steps.label: 2.1: Data Types and Variables
steps.content:
Text-based Programming

2.1: Data Types and Variables

Year 7

  • Today: write programs as text, and store values in them.
  • The big question: why does a program need to know what kind of value it stores?
Think → Pair → ShareA game shows your score going up. Where does the computer keep that score while you play? Why must it be able to change?Show the answer

It keeps it in its memory, under a name. Every time you score, the program changes the value it stores. Today we learn how.

steps.label: Programs Written as Text
steps.content:
Programs Written as Text

Think → Pair → SharePredict: what does this program show on the screen? Why are the words in quote marks?Show the worked answer

Hello, then Bye on the next line. The quote marks show Python where the text starts and ends.

Python is a programming language. We type each instruction as a line of text.

print("Hello")
print("Bye")
  • print shows a message on the screen, like a Say box.
  • The text goes inside quote marks.
  • Python runs the lines in order, from the top.

steps.label: A Variable Stores a Value
steps.content:
A Variable Stores a Value

Think → Pair → SharePredict: what is the difference between print(score) and print("score")? Why?Show the worked answer

print(score) shows 5, the value stored in score. print("score") shows the word score, because quote marks mean the text itself.

A variable is a named store in the computer's memory. It holds one value.

score = 5
print(score)
score5
  • = means store: put 5 in the variable called score.
  • print(score) shows the value stored in score.

steps.label: Store a New Value
steps.content:
Store a New Value

Think → Pair → SharePredict: what does this program print? Why?Show the worked answer

It prints 8. A variable holds one value at a time, so storing 8 replaces the 5. There is only one print, at the end. That is why it is called a variable: its value can vary.

Predict first. Then the teacher shows the answer.

score = 5
score = 8
print(score)
  • Line 1 stores 5 in score.
  • Line 2 stores 8 in score.
  • There is one print, at the end.

steps.label: Change a Variable Using Its Own Value
steps.content:
Change a Variable Using Its Own Value

Think → Pair → SharePredict: what does this program print? Why is coins = coins + 5 not a maths mistake?Show the worked answer

It prints 15. In Python = does not mean "is the same as". It means: work out the right side, then store the answer in the variable on the left.

Predict first. Then the teacher shows the answer.

coins = 10
coins = coins + 5
print(coins)
  • In Python, + adds, - takes away, * times and / divides.
  • best = coins stores a copy of the value in coins in best.
  • This is how a game adds to a score.

items.prompt: What does each program print, and why?
options: A prints 8 and B prints 5: B prints before the change
Both print 8: both programs have the same lines
A prints 5 and B prints 8: the last line runs first
Both print 5: score = 5 is the first line in both
items.explain: Lines run in order. A changes score to 8, then prints. B prints while score is still 5, and changes it after.

steps.label: Three Data Types
steps.content:
Three Data Types

Think → Pair → ShareWhy is "12" a String, but 12 an Integer?Show the answer

The quote marks. Inside quote marks Python stores the characters as text, even when they are digits.

A data type is the kind of value a variable stores.

Data typeIn PythonIt storesExamples
Integerinta whole number12   -3   0
Realfloata number with a decimal point2.5   -0.75   4.0
Stringstrtext, in quote marks"Mia"   "12"
  • / means divide. It always gives a Real: 8 / 2 is 4.0.
  • A whole number and a Real together give a Real: 3 + 0.5 is 3.5.

steps.label: Your Turn: Which Data Type?
steps.content:
Your Turn: Which Data Type?

Think → Pair → ShareWhy does Python need to know the kind of value it stores?Show the answer

The kind of value decides what Python can do with it: numbers can be worked out, text cannot.

Type Integer, Real or String for the value each line stores.

Total: 4 marks

steps.label: Compare: 5 + 5 or "5" + "5"?
steps.content:
Compare: 5 + 5 or "5" + "5"?

Think → Pair → ShareBoth programs use the same + sign. How can they print different things?Show the answer

Talk in pairs about what is different between the two lines. Then choose your answer.

Program A

print(5 + 5)

Program B

print("5" + "5")

items.prompt: What does each program print, and why?
options: A prints 10 and B prints 55: B joins two Strings
A prints 10 and B prints 10: + always adds numbers
A prints 55 and B prints 10: quote marks add numbers
A prints 10 and B stops: Strings cannot use +
items.explain: In A, 5 and 5 are Integers, so + adds them: 10. In B, "5" and "5" are Strings, so + joins them: 55.

steps.label: Why the Data Type Matters
steps.content:
Why the Data Type Matters

Think → Pair → SharePredict: is a score in a game an Integer, a Real or a String? Why?Show the worked answer

An Integer. It is a whole number, and the game adds to it.

Choose the data type from what the value is and what the program does with it.

  • The data type decides what + does: Integers add, Strings join.
  • A Real keeps the part after the decimal point: a price of 2.5 stays 2.5.
  • A phone number is a String: it starts with 0, and we never add phone numbers.
  • A name is always a String.

steps.label: Explain: Choose the Data Type
steps.content:
Explain: Choose the Data Type

Think → Pair → ShareWhat makes an explanation worth 2 marks?Show the answer

Two connected points: what is wrong now, and what to use instead, joined with "so" or "because".

A program stores a pupil's height of 1.52 metres as height = 1.

items.prompt: Explain why this data type is wrong for the height, and say which data type to use. [2]
scheme: 1 is an Integer / a whole number, so the part after the decimal point (.52) is lost
Use a Real (float), because a height has a decimal point / 1.52
items.guidance: Award 1 mark for each point. Accept float for Real and int for Integer. Do not accept "it is a number" alone for either mark.
items.modelAnswer: height = 1 is an Integer, so the .52 is lost (1 mark). Use a Real (float), because 1.52 has a decimal point (1 mark).
